text: Write it down, get some sleep, and go back over it with one grounded person once your head is clear.
section: No Rash Actions: Visions Are Not Commands
reader: someone during or just after an overwhelming trip, from a drug or a practice, who feels a vision is telling them to act

sentences.s: Write it down, get some sleep, and go back over it with one grounded person once your head is clear.
sentences.payoff: they put a vision's command off: write it down, sleep, and talk it over with one grounded person once their head is clear, whether it came from a drug or a practice
sentences.follows: it is the section's rule in bold, after the heading (Visions Are Not Commands): what to do instead of acting

placement: No Rash Actions: Visions Are Not Commands, its bold rule, before the paragraph on treating trip content as experience-content

opens.first_sentence: Write it down, get some sleep, and go back over it with one grounded person once your head is clear.
opens.why_reading: it tells someone who feels a vision is telling them to act what to do instead, right away

same_point: the next paragraph ends "it can wait until the state has passed", the reason for this rule, and the list before it says "Until you have slept and eaten, maybe don't ...": they make the rule's point from two sides, none merged

needed.reader: a fresh Haiku agent that saw only the paragraph, its heading and what it is for, given tools/humanization/needed_read_brief.md (NEEDED-READ.md)

questions.Q1: PASS: it opens on what to do
questions.Q2: PASS: each step is something the reader does, and the heading says what they are for
questions.Q3: PASS: "once your head is clear" fits a state from a practice, which "sober" didn't
questions.Q4: PASS: no term a reader wouldn't know
questions.Q6: PASS: write it down, sleep, then talk it over: the order they happen in
questions.Q7: PASS: for someone in that state now

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
